doc.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001

title: An imagined future song about grace and balance
summary: Asked for a story not yet set to music, she says it would be about grace and finding balance after giving her life to music.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You told us about stories. You sang the song for us “When You Were Nine Years Old.” That song just transported me. I thought I was going to come out of my chair. Because it was so vivid. It was so descriptive and beautiful and alive. Tell us a story that you haven’t put to melody yet.

Let’s say it’s 2004 and you’ve traveled all over the world and sung all different kind of places, and you’re going to an album and you’re going to tell us another story. Tell us about this one. Just take me there in your imagination.

Well I think that the first word that comes to my mind is grace. I think the story would be about maybe where I am right now, how I feel and how I view life right now. Because there are a lot of things that are happening, like I’ve given my life to music. I’ve created a kind of imbalance in my life because I haven’t really given much to my personal life. Now I need to know what that’s about, and I want to write about that journey of finding that balance. And grace has a lot to do with that. Living in a state of grace.
I’ll ask you one more question.
I’ve never had anybody ask me that but that’s a good one.
I go some strange places too.
That’s okay, I like it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
